problem: One hundred people are in line to see a movie. Each person wants to sit in the front row, which contains one hundred seats, and each has a favorite seat, chosen randomly and independently. They enter the row one at a time from the far right. As they walk, if they reach their favorite seat, they sit, but to avoid stepping over people, if they encounter a person already seated, they sit to that person's right. This has probability: $$P(n)=\frac{100-(n-1)}{100} \cdot \frac{100-(n-2)}{100} \cdots \frac{100}{100}=\frac{100!}{(100-n)!\cdot 100^{n}}$$ The probability, $Q(n)$, that exactly $n$ people sit is $$P(n)-P(n+1)=\frac{100!}{(100-n)!\cdot 100^{n}}-\frac{100!}{(99-n)!\cdot 100^{n+1}}=\frac{100!\cdot n}{(100-n)!\cdot 100^{n+1}}$$ Now, $$\frac{Q(n)}{Q(n-1)}=\frac{100!\cdot n}{(100-n)!\cdot 100^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{(101-n)!\cdot 100^{n}}{100!\cdot(n-1)}=\frac{n(101-n)}{100(n-1)}=\frac{101 n-n^{2}}{100 n-100}$$ which is greater than 1 exactly when $n^{2}-n-100<0$, that is, for $n \leq 10$. Therefore, the maximum value of $Q(n)$ occurs for $n=10$.
